comments.author: @VijayRagMalimNawar
comments.text: India has endured generations of hardship shaped in part by the wealth and resources stolen and looted during the East India Company and British colonial era. Yet India’s story is not defined by suffering, but by resilience, renewal, and determination. The wheel of karma turns slowly, but it never forgets. Justice need not come through revenge, but through prosperity, dignity, and the rise of a people who refuse to be defined by their past. What was diminished can be rebuilt, and what was taken cannot extinguish India’s spirit. India will continue to rise, overcome its challenges, and shape its own destiny.

comments.text: India is country of over 700 million females, the highest population in the world, they have very separate roles to their male counterparts, same as other cultures and their lives involve much more colourful and beautiful vibes and sights like family time, shadis and festivals to name a few. Why don't you film more videos that involve women and girls side of life instead of men working in a slum? Like maybe a Kalash Yatra in a Bihar village (I saw one yesterday called Saraswati Puja Kalash Yatra in Darbhanga district), there are millions like this, or a Navratri Garba in a Gujarati village, so many people live stream things from their villages, Bakharla is one example that always puts out it's Navratri festival amongst many others. The heart of India is in it's villages, where 65% of it's 1.4 billion people live, it's much more family orientated as it reflects general life and girls are generally more domestic than their male counterparts. Each state has it's own variety of peoples, festivals, languages, and traditions. Festivals are especially beautiful, vibrant and lively with music, noise and huge crowds of women and girls with long flowing hair and bright, sparkling colourful clothes, dancing in unison. It's like a never ending sea of beauty and colours, their clothes make everywhere you look seem like a kaleidoscope.
